purpose: Test the hypothesis left open by E162 (effective rank 8/256): is the low rank of the raw-EEG encoder the bottleneck for the cross-session diagnostic AUC? Only the encoder structure and the pooling are changed, keeping the two E162 wins (no output L2 normalisation, dual-perturbation-family cross-session invariance). The E143 open-set protocol is reused verbatim and the E65 control must still reproduce W = 0.6958 / diagnostic AUC = 0.7578.
hypothesis: Raising the effective rank (removing BatchNorm and reducing pooling strength) lifts the diagnostic AUC above the E143/E65 value 0.7578; E159 requires diagnostic AUC ~0.93 for W > 0.80.
changes_vs_E162: BatchNorm removed everywhere (batch statistics are a cross-domain instability); replaced by GroupNorm(8 groups, affine, per-sample statistics) in every conv block

pooling strength reduced in three ways: variant A = learnable-query attention pooling (4 queries x 128 ch = 512), variant B = global mean||max pooling with no final linear compression (256 ch -> 512), variant C = multi-scale time pooling (4 segments x 128 ch = 512)
variant D = E162 encoder structure kept (mean||max -> Linear) but BN -> GroupNorm, used only to isolate the BN-removal effect from the pooling change
lambda_VICReg fixed at 0.0 (E162 showed it is harmful) and temperature fixed at 0.1; no further sweep
eval PCA grid extended to 32/64/128/256 (E162 used 32/64/96) because the embeddings are now 512-d
kept_from_E162: no L2 normalisation of the output embedding
dual disjoint perturbation families (A = channel gain + electrode drift, B = band amplitude reweighting + additive noise) of the same trial must map to the same embedding (MSE invariance weight 1.0)
identical training protocol: SupCon over within-task identity labels, cosine LR with warmup, early stopping on the 0.6<frac<=0.8 Train block, fit rows = frac<=0.6, >0.8 never used
identical open-set evaluation protocol (task standardisation -> PCA on fit rows -> k prototypes -> 5-block Train OOF threshold -> LOSO excluding the scored identity -> Test scoring only)

variants.name: B_stack256_nolinear_gn512
variants.label: global mean||max pooling, no final linear compression (256 ch -> 512)

variants.name: D_e162head_gn256
variants.label: E162 structure control: mean||max -> Linear(256) with GroupNorm instead of BatchNorm

encoder.normalisation: per-trial per-channel mean removal, then division by the per-trial global RMS (fixed, no batch statistics)
encoder.output: no L2 normalisation, no BatchNorm, no loss on the raw embedding scale
encoder.note_B: the pre-registration text said 'conv channels widened to 128' but also 'output 512-d'; mean||max of 128 channels is 256, so the last conv is widened to 256 to honour the 512-d requirement without a linear compression

train.loss: SupCon over within-task identity labels (both perturbation families as views) + 1.0 * MSE(viewA, viewB); lambda_VICReg = 0
train.valid_metric: mean per-task leave-half-out nearest-centroid identity accuracy on the 0.6<frac<=0.8 block (Train only)

view_A_electrode.drift_sine_weight: U(-0.8, 0.8) * amplitude, 0.5-3 cycles per trial, random phase

augment.note: identical to E162; the two families are disjoint by design

protocol.loso_known_block: 0.6 < frac <= 0.8, prototypes from fit_rows (frac <= 0.6) of the 19 enrolled identities
protocol.threshold: 5-block Train OOF score quantile at each acceptance rate; LOSO uses per-fold known-block quantile

e159_reference.note: with the E143 scores frozen and the threshold swept, the best W is 0.6971 and the optimistic upper bound 0.7352

reporting.test_official: N/A: Test has no public labels; session is used only for the diagnostic AUC after scoring
reporting.effective_rank: number of principal components of the task-standardised fit-row embeddings needed for 95% / 99% cumulative variance
